title: Dataset and Replication Package for M-11: Auditing Synthetic Risk Labels and Physical Baselines in a Cyber-Physical Benchmark for Underground Mining
description:
Overview:

This repository hosts the official replication package, synthetic benchmark dataset, and experimental audit assets for the study "M-11: Auditing Synthetic Risk Labels and Physical Baselines in a Cyber-Physical Benchmark for Underground Mining" (submitted to Acta Montanistica Slovaca, 2026).

M-11 is a simulation-only cyber-physical benchmark that integrates AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance attributes with synthetic kinematic positioning, physiological, and environmental indicators (10,000 records; 37 columns) to audit the statistical and architectural mechanics of synthetic risk labelling in confined underground mining.

Key Empirical Findings Reported in the Paper:

  • Label Circularity Audit: Variance decomposition demonstrates that 82.07% of the synthetic score variance is driven by spatial/kinematic components, 17.43% by injected noise, 0.48% by multimodal variables, and 0.02% by cross-covariance.
  • Symmetric Holdout Evaluation (n = 2,000, seed 42): Calibrated Time-to-Collision (TTC) and Random Forest both achieve F2 = 0.9103; XGBoost achieves F2 = 0.9065. The paired bootstrap difference (ΔF2 = -0.0038, 95% CI: -0.0129 to 0.0047) and Holm-adjusted McNemar test (p = 0.6015) confirm no statistically significant gap under circular labels.
  • Decoupled Hazard Stress Tests: Under 22% class prevalence and low signal-to-noise ratio, non-spatial decoupled labels (CO, fatigue, vibration) push F2 optimisation to near-universal HIGH alerts, approaching the trivial Always-HIGH baseline (F2 = 0.5851). A multimodal-only composite target recovers F2 = 0.6408 with 54.1% specificity.
  • Feature Ablations: Removing three direct kinematic indicators reduces F2 by 9.60 percentage points; removing the entire 8-feature spatial block reduces F2 by 32.52 percentage points from the full 0.9065 baseline.
  • Computational Performance: Local backend P95 latency scales to 27.91 ms under 500 concurrent agents (< 200 ms supervisory threshold). The WebGL/Three.js integrated-GPU prototype achieves 34.8 FPS under nominal load.
  • Deterministic Safety & GenAI Audit: The independent deterministic safety layer satisfies 17 automated unit/integration tests and 100/100 scripted regulatory scenario checks. The Gemini language model acts strictly as an exploratory natural-language interface without numerical autonomy.

Package Contents & Verification Checksums (SHA-256):

  • public_mining_equipment_dataset.csv (3,859,401 bytes) — SHA-256: b71d0b6baed8b6e0bc7eee1a1a5b7440d06a04ddaea5d502907cf03d958705f0
  • requirements.txt (574 bytes) — Frozen Python 3.10.11 scientific dependencies.
  • results/feature_dictionary.csv — Full dictionary defining all 37 attributes, physical units, and provenance.
  • results/label_circularity_audit.json — Variance decomposition and baseline comparison exports.
  • results/genai_audit_bank.json — 100 structured synthetic scenarios for LLM compliance auditing.
  • results/genai_audit_review_sheet.csv — Manual verification rubric with inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.85).

Boundary of Scope:

M-11 is a computational simulation benchmark and exploratory advisory prototype. It does not establish mine-site functional safety, nor does it claim active-mine physical twin synchronisation or autonomous braking actuation.
